business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Dilutive Revenue-Based Financing for Digital Brands

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014, Cap. 100 (Laws of Gibraltar) — ss. 5, 39–51 (registration, memorandum & articles), s. 96 (certificate of incorporation); Income Tax Act 2010 ss. 40 & 44A (non-resident exempt/gross-asset election); Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (AML registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Registry, H.M. Government of Gibraltar (via eRegistrar online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO-01 Application for Registration of a Company together with Memorandum of Association, Articles of Association, Statement of Initial Share Capital, and Statement of Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum under Gibraltar law; practical floor of one (1) fully paid ordinary share of GBP 1.00 at incorporation; no escrow or deposit account requirement; authorized capital typically GBP 1,000
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriber's subscription of one fully paid ordinary share in the initial issued share capital of the Company be and is hereby approved, effective upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation by the Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be established at the registered address as filed with the Registrar through the licensed corporate services provider. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] be appointed Chief Executive Director and [Secretary Name] be appointed Corporate Secretary, jointly authorized to open bank accounts, execute revenue-based financing agreements, and file statutory returns. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the enclosed Corporate Governance Charter and Revenue-Based Financing Underwriting Policy be adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name clearance and jurisdiction check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies — Companies House Registry (eRegistrar online portal), Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name reservation request for the fund vehicle, verify absence of identical or confusingly similar names, and confirm that the proposed name contains no restricted words (e.g. 'Bank', 'Trust') requiring GFSC consent. Reserve approved name for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Cover letter from licensed corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If query is raised, submit an alternative name list and a written explanation of the proposed business purpose; escalation to the Registrar under s. 33 Companies Act 2014 for an administrative review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscriber KYC, due diligence, and constitutional document preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed fiduciary / registered agent approved by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect complete AML/CFT due diligence on each subscriber, director, and secretary, including notarized passports, proof of residential address, and banker's references. Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association, consents to act, and registered office consent; arrange notarization and apply for the Director's police certificate where residency is in Gibraltar.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association (Table A based, with revenue-based financing objects)
Form of Consent to Act as Director
Form of Consent to Act as Secretary
Notarized KYC pack (passport, address proof, bank reference)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries document notarization or language, rectify by re-execution before a Gibraltar Notary Public and resubmit via eRegistrar with a statutory declaration of compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies — Companies House Registry, H.M. Government of Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File electronically through the eRegistrar portal: Form CO-01, statement of initial share capital, statement of proposed registered office, and the executed constitutional documents. Pay the registration fee and stamp duty by credit transfer. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with a company registration number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For registry queries on capital structure or objects clause, submit a supplemental declaration and amended articles within 14 days; express review available on payment of an expedited fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and exempt status application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: HM Commissioner of Income Tax, Gibraltar; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (AML Supervision)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN) and file the election under the Income Tax Act 2010 s. 40/s. 44A for exemption or gross-asset treatment of foreign-source financing income. Separately register the company with the GFSC AML Hub under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015, appoint a Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and adopt the AML Compliance Manual.
required_dossiers: Income Tax Act exemption/gross-asset election template
MLRO and Compliance Officer appointment letters
AML Risk Assessment and Business Risk Profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to any tax office substantive questions within 14 days, providing a legal opinion on the financing fund's economic substance (minimum 8% core income generation and physical presence in Gibraltar).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational board governance and bank activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company; licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational board meeting by written resolution; adopt the First Board Resolution, approve the issuing of the share certificate, order the company seal, open a corporate bank account with a Gibraltar-licensed bank or EMI, and establish the statutory registers and minute book.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (as set out in the legal framework section)
Share certificate and register of members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank defers account opening, provide an AML/Economic Substance clarification letter, the GFSC registration certificate, and a board certified copy of the financing fund mandate; escalate to the bank's compliance committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the activity is non-industrial professional financing; premises oversight falls under the Building Control Office, H.M. Government of Gibraltar, for serviced office occupancy only
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or operating license required for ISIC 6499 revenue-based financing; mandatory registration is limited to GFSC AML under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change, H.M. Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — registration only; no full EIA mandated for pure office-based financing activity with no manufacturing or emission sources
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero industrial discharges; general compliance with the Environmental Protection Act 2006 for waste disposal, Gibraltar water utility discharge conditions, and the Waste Framework Regulations for confidential document shredding.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service under the Fire Safety (Premises) Regulations; annual inspection of emergency exits, extinguishers, and alarm panels; structural load certificate for the records/filing room; workplace clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar) with a mandatory risk assessment and employer's liability insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar, Income Tax Office — official portal: MyTaxGIB (https://tax.gibraltar.gov.gi) and Gibraltar Companies Registry (https://www.gibraltarcompaniesregistry.gi)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Bermuda Exempted Company seeking Gibraltar tax identity must first register as a foreign company with the Gibraltar Companies Registry (CR number acts as the corporate TIN). Thereafter, file Form PA1 (Application for Taxpayer Identification) with the Income Tax Office via MyTaxGIB. If the company is managed and controlled from Gibraltar, it will be treated as Gibraltar tax resident and issued a TIN; if not resident, a TIN is still issued for Gibraltar-source income reporting. No VAT ID is issued because Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT territory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar does not operate a check-the-box election regime. Under the Income Tax Act 2010, a foreign company may elect to be assessed on a territorial basis if treated as non-resident; hybrid mismatch alignment elections are available under the Taxation (Hybrid Mismatch) Regulations 2017. For a Bermuda Exempted Company, the default classification remains tax-exempt in Bermuda, but Gibraltar tax residence follows central management and control; no special Gibraltar fund election abolishes the need for substance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Nil in Gibraltar pounds (GIP). Gibraltar imposes no VAT or GST and therefore no economic turnover threshold for VAT registration. Customs import duty obligations arise on the physical importation of goods regardless of turnover; an EORI number is mandatory for customs declarations, but is not turnover-based.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar has no real-time fiscal invoicing or digital stamping mandate. Tax returns and company filings are submitted digitally through MyTaxGIB and the Companies Registry e-portal. Customs entries are cleared through the ASYCUDA World electronic declaration system with real-time risk profiling; regulated financial transactions are separately reported under Gibraltar AML regulations through MLROS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: No VAT/GST zero-rating claim is possible under Gibraltar law because Gibraltar does not levy VAT or GST. Outbound royalty-financing, revenue-based financing, and associated fund services are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax. For physical goods moving through Gibraltar, relief may be available only for goods in transit/warehousing under the Customs Ordinance on a suspension basis, not as a refundable export zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD or ASYCUDA entry)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or FX confirmation for repatriated proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Although no VAT zero-rating exists, fraudulent claims to customs or tax exemption attract clawback of any excise/import duty relieved, fines up to £3,000 per offence, interest at 36% per annum applied by the Collector, and imprisonment of up to seven years under the Income Tax Act 2010 and Criminal Offences (Money Laundering) law. Where a fund misrepresents its Gibraltar tax-exempt status, the Income Tax Officer may retrospectively revoke the tax exemption and assess tax for up to six prior years together with penalty surcharges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England as the sterling monetary authority; Government of Gibraltar as issuer of the Gibraltar pound tied at parity to GBP; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission as the financial conduct and AML/CFT supervisory authority; HM Treasury as the United Kingdom sanctions authority applicable to Gibraltar-linked sterling clearing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar has no exchange-control mechanism and no material convertibility restriction. The Gibraltar pound is fully convertible at a 1:1 peg to sterling, and both current-account flows (royalty income, financing fees, operating costs) and capital-account flows (equity subscription, shareholder loans, intercompany advances, profit distributions) may be converted and remitted freely. Profit remittance hurdles are non-FX in nature: the principal challenges are demonstrated economic substance, AML source-of-funds validation, sanctions screening, CRS/tax reporting, and arm's-length pricing of the royalty-financing arrangements. A Bermuda Exempted Company should maintain clear central-management-and-control evidence in Gibraltar to prevent adverse tax and substance challenges.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion ratios, or fixed conversion deadlines in Gibraltar or the United Kingdom. Export and trade receipts may be retained in the original currency and repatriated at the treasury's discretion. Banks may be required to report balance-of-payments statistics for large cross-border receipts, and proceeds originating from high-risk or non-convertible jurisdictions require enhanced due diligence.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and segregated treasury settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, but only as an auxiliary collection and disbursement layer. A non-Gibraltar digital EMI or e-money institution, including a UK FCA-authorised EMI, may provide GBP and EUR virtual IBANs, open-banking collection rails, and direct-debit initiation; however, it is not a clearing participant in CHAPS, RTGS, or the Gibraltar sterling clearing network and cannot serve as the sole principal settlement bank for fund capital. Legal constraints include GFSC expectations that regulated treasury activity maintain a substantive banking relationship with a licensed Gibraltar bank, safeguarding rules for e-money funds, limits on onward payment risk, and sanctions-screening obligations. Use of an offshore EMI is therefore limited to ancillary receivables collection with daily sweeps to a Tier 1 Gibraltar bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar does not statutorily require a physical meeting for corporate account opening, but the GFSC AML/CFT framework allows risk-based face-to-face or certified electronic identification. For a Bermuda Exempted Company with limited operating history, the practical mandate is an enhanced KYC interview: at least one executive director or ultimate beneficial owner must undergo a live video interview with bank-grade biometric liveness verification. Physical attendance is likely to be required if the applicant has no prior relationship, no independent Gibraltar substance, or complex multi-tier offshore ownership. A notarised and apostilled board resolution, full UBO declaration, and a Gibraltar registered-office certificate materially accelerate onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident offshore exempted company lacking local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed board minutes showing Gibraltar management decisions; Gibraltar registered office/agent agreement; group structure chart; economic substance rationale for royalty-financing activities; audited or management accounts; tax-residency position paper; and CV/passport copies of Gibraltar directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in source of wealth for the inbound capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed subscription agreement or deed of contribution; source-of-funds letters from investors; bank statements evidencing accumulation of funds; liquidation or sale-and-purchase documents if funds derive from a corporate exit; solvency certificate of the lending shareholder; and a consolidated treasury funding model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty/financing cash-flow patterns creating round-tripping or thin-capitalisation red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent IP or royalty valuation report; transfer-pricing documentation under the OECD TNMM or CUP method; executed royalty financing agreements; loan and repayment schedules; debt-to-equity ratio calculation; projections of cash flows; and legal opinion confirming legitimate financing purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list, PEP, or adverse-media match on an ultimate beneficial owner or major counterparty
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Same-name explanation and identity evidence; passport and proof-of-address documents; PEP declaration and politically exposed person assessment; independent adverse-media search; sanctions screening results; and confirmation from an independent compliance advisor that no HM Treasury, OFAC, or EU sanctions action blocks the relationship.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route through a licensed Tier 1 Gibraltar bank using SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own banking relationship, with a clear reference to the underlying instrument. For equity capital, the purpose should be mapped to the UK balance-of-payments 'direct investment equity' category and the beneficiary payment reference should identify 'GB__GI__BM_EXEMPTED_CO__ISIC_6499_10_ROYALTY_FINANCING_FUND / Additional Paid-In Capital'. For shareholder loans, use the purpose category for 'intra-group financing' and include the executed loan agreement number. The receiving bank will verify the corporate board resolution, updated capital table, source-of-funds evidence, UBO declarations, and non-circumvention of sanctions. Telegraphic transfers above an enhanced threshold should be pre-agreed with the bank's treasury desk to avoid prolonged compliance holds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 is the primary clearing rail for royalty disbursements and financing advances. For same-day GBP obligations, CHAPS through a UK clearer is appropriate; for EUR payments to European counterparties, use SEPA Credit Transfer where the Gibraltar bank maintains SEPA access. High-value or dual-beneficiary treasury movements may require MT202 cover through a correspondent bank. Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT720) are permitted for goods-backed or security-backed trades, but the royalty-financing fund should avoid trade-finance documentary descriptions that do not match the underlying revenue-based financing instrument. Each outgoing instruction must carry the contract or invoice reference and an accurate purpose code; no transaction may be structured to avoid AML reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward contracts in GBP, EUR, and USD for committed royalty-financing cash flows
FX spot transactions for operational liquidity conversion
FX swaps for temporary current-account liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps for matching long-dated financing assets and funding liabilities
Vanilla FX options for asymmetric treasury risk management
Non-deliverable forwards for eligible non-convertible or restricted currencies where the underlying income stream creates a genuine commercial exposure
Currency-linked escrow and forward-prepaid structures where the bank's credit and AML appetite permits

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return and Annual Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation; annual fee covers the January to December Government license year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% per month of arrears; continued default beyond 12 months triggers administrative strike-off of the exempted company and forfeiture of Bermuda tax-exempt status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Economic Substance (International Tax Compliance) Annual Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies - International Tax Compliance Unit, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year (e.g., 30 June following a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial penalty of BMD 10,000 plus BMD 10,000 per month of continued non-compliance up to BMD 100,000; penalties up to BMD 50,000 for false declarations; criminal liability for directors knowingly submitting false information; information exchange with HMRC may be activated.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% Gibraltar corporation tax rate applicable to chargeable profits of a Gibraltar-resident company or a non-resident company through a Gibraltar permanent establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No codified tax holidays; the Bermuda Exempted Company remains tax-exempt on worldwide profits not sourced in Gibraltar, and only Gibraltar-source profits are taxable at 12.5%; preferential deductions apply to arm's-length financing costs, royalty expense under the royalty financing model, and any qualifying research and development expenditure; tax losses may be carried forward for five years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CIT-1 (Company Income Tax Return); filed electronically through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office (ITO) e-Services portal under the Income Tax Act 2010.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one CIT-1 return per accounting period; quarterly payments on account may be required when tax exceeds GBP 100,000).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within twelve months after the end of the accounting period; the tax balance must be paid on or before the first day of the ninth month after the period end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company tax reference number and legal name of the Bermuda Exempted Company as registered in Bermuda and, if applicable, the Gibraltar branch registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Bermuda company number and the Gibraltar 'Overseas Company' registration number if a PE or branch has been established in Gibraltar.
For a newly registered foreign entity, use the date of commencement of Gibraltar-source business activity.
Match the Bermuda Exempted Company's financial statements; if a Gibraltar PE, align with the PE's statutory accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gibraltar-source trading profits and chargeable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose only profits attributable to the Gibraltar PE or deriving from Gibraltar contracts; exclude passive foreign royalty income earned by the Bermuda parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenditure, including any excessive royalty or financing payments to related parties not meeting the arm's length standard.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Bermuda Exempted Company is the foreign lender or IP holder, disclose all intercompany payments received from the Gibraltar operating entity and certify arm's length pricing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward and utilised (maximum five-year carry-forward).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company may only utilise losses attributable to the same trade carried on in Gibraltar; foreign losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing documentation declaration (if aggregate controlled transactions exceed the GBP 1,000,000 threshold).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the royalty financing arrangement, the legal owner of the IP, and the funding source; state that a Local File and Master File are maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Economic Substance (ES) confirmation code under the Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select 'Relevant Activity — Finance and Leasing' or 'Investment Fund Management' if the royalty financing fund operates as a fund; confirm physical presence and management in Gibraltar.
Calculate tax only on taxable Gibraltar-source profits; if no PE or no Gibraltar-source income, enter zero but still file if required.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic GBP 500 penalty and daily GBP 50 surcharge up to a maximum of GBP 3,000; tax understatement from carelessness incurs 30% of the unpaid tax, from deliberate accounting 100%; interest runs at 8% per annum from the due date until settlement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Gibraltar imposes no withholding tax on dividend distributions under domestic law).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since the domestic rate is nil, no DTA relief is necessary for dividends paid from Gibraltar; where a treaty elsewise applies (e.g., UK-Gibraltar DTA, Malta-Gibraltar DTA), the non-resident shareholder desiring a nil or reduced rate must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its tax authority, submit it to the Gibraltar paying agent before payment, and complete Form DTA-D1; the paying agent then remits the gross amount and records the exemption in the annual withholding tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory Gibraltar WHT and 0% under the Gibraltar DTA network (including UK); interest: 0% statutory and 0% treaty; this nil rate applies to cross-border royalty fees and debt financing interest paid by the Gibraltar operating entity to the Bermuda Exempted Company.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File are required where the value of cross-border controlled transactions exceeds GBP 1,000,000 in a fiscal year; Country-by-Country Reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar's Economic Substance (Company and Branches) Regulations 2020 impose a real-presence test on 'relevant activities', including finance and leasing and fund management. The royalty financing fund must demonstrate: (a) adequate physical offices and employees in Gibraltar; (b) locally conducted core income-generating activities; (c) all board meetings and strategic decisions made in Gibraltar. Failure to meet these tests, or omission of the annual ES return, exposes the entity to sanctions up to GBP 10,000 plus daily default fines and possible strike-off; the Bermuda Exempted Company cannot rely on its Bermuda tax-exempt status to avoid Gibraltar ESR obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate suppression of Gibraltar-source profits from royalty financing; use of artificial round-tripping or sham invoices to shift profits to Bermuda; claiming fictitious deductions for royalty or interest payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A penalty of 100% of the under-documented tax plus interest at 8% per annum; criminal prosecution under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act and Proceeds of Crime Act; fine up to GBP 50,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years for responsible officers; forfeiture of the underlying assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may personally owe civil restitution for the avoided tax; are subject to travel bans preventing attendance at board meetings abroad; disqualification as director for up to 15 years in the UK/Gibraltar; extradition to UK courts where the conduct affects UK tax residence; custodial sentence for fraud and money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the royalty financing fund wholly from Bermuda with no physical presence in Gibraltar; using mailbox directors; failing to file Economic Substance Return; failing to record the ultimate beneficial owner on the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations and Companies Act 2014, regulatory fines up to GBP 25,000; daily default fine of GBP 1,000 for continued non-compliance; compulsory strike-off of the overseas branch and loss of Gibraltar trading rights; the company may be placed on the GFIU public warning list.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are liable for the unpaid penalties personally; a compliance failure may be treated as an unwarranted defense of the corporate veil, allowing Gibraltar courts to pierce the veil and order personal asset confiscation; travel bans and prohibition of re-entry are available where the director personally facilitated the shell structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving royalty or financing receipts through Direct Debit/ACH or wire transfers without customer due diligence, source-of-funds verification, or suspicious activity reporting; structuring payments to avoid the Gibraltar AML reporting threshold; using unlicensed EMI or banking rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime Act (Gibraltar) and the Financial Services Ordinance, failure to file a suspicious activity report carries criminal liability with fines not limited in value and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties of up to GBP 5 million from the GFIU; freezing orders and forfeiture of any monies linked to the violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who knowingly process illicit payments or fail to implement an AML program may be criminally convicted personally, disgraced, and barred from any Gibraltar financial administration; travel bans, extradition requests, and personal civil liability for investor losses can be enforced in UK courts; the corporate indemnity clause does not protect acting directors.
